meaning.text: Afanasyev glosses the name Sirin as equal to 'siren' (сирена).

peoples_regions.region: "наше простонародье" (our common people), who came to know the bird through popular prints
"нашей старинной символикѣ" (our old symbolism); carvings of the Dmitrievsky cathedral in Vladimir on the Klyazma

appearance_forms.label: Afanasyev's paradise bird of the popular prints and old symbolism
Human-shaped pair of the old Hamartolos translation

appearance.text: Is a paradise bird (райская птица), named together with the Alkonost.
In the old translation of George Hamartolos, the beings called sirins are described as human-shaped creatures.
In that translation they appear as a pair, a man and a woman.

scene.text: Shown in popular prints (лубочныя картины), through which the common people came to know it.
According to Count Uvarov, the Sirin and the Alkonost are found on the carvings of the Dmitrievsky cathedral in Vladimir on the Klyazma.
In the old translation of George Hamartolos, the human-shaped pair called sirins were seen in the river Nile when the sun had risen.

behavior_habitat.text: In old Russian symbolism the paradise birds Alkonost and Sirin often signify the righteous.

notes.text: Every afanasyev1868:p.135 claim (the native form, the 'Sirin = siren' gloss, the popular prints, 'our common people') comes from footnote 2 at the foot of the page, not the body text. The footnote is explanatory prose, not a bare reference, so it was used; the verify agent should decide whether it counts. The OCR reads 'Сиринъ иг сирена'; 'иг' is taken as an equals sign.

afanasyev1869:p.153 is a passage about the vily: Afanasyev says the old translation of George Hamartolos identifies the vily with sirens, and quotes it naming two human-shaped beings in the Nile 'иже и сирины нарицаются, рекше вилы' (OCR 'рен-те'). The human-shaped form and the Nile scene are attributed to the sirin only because the quoted text gives them that name; they may belong to the classical sirens rather than the paradise bird.
The 'signify the righteous' clause is symbolism rather than behaviour; it is filed under behavior_habitat for want of a better field.

names.variants: no source gives another name for the sirin; the plural 'сирины' (afanasyev1869:p.153) is the same name. Searched sirin, сирин, сирином, сирина, сиринъ, сирины, sirine, siren, сирен in all sources.
dealing_with_it: no page gives wards, offerings, taboos or escapes. Same searches as above, plus алконост, 'paradise bird', 'bird of paradise'.

origin: no page says where the sirin comes from. afanasyev1868:p.135 says only that popular prints made the bird known to the common people; that is the transmission of the image, not an origin of the creature. Same searches as above.
variants: no page describes the sirin differently by people or region. Same searches as above.
